correctness.rationale: In Smith coordinates the right factor has form D_{k-a}H after the coordinate change, because Ann(pi^a)=pi^{k-a}R including levels 0 and k. The middle product Y=D_a S D_{k-a} is supported only on a_i<a_j. At any h its entries are covered by the rows a_i<h and columns a_j>h. Splitting into those two blocks factors YH through a free module of rank n-n_h, proving the upper bound without confusing image generators with reduction rank or minors. For an independent sharpness argument, sort the levels and write m=max n_h. Pair row i with column i+m for 1<=i<=n-m; a_{i+m}>a_i since no equal-level block has m+1 entries. Put ones at any t of these pairs in S and take H=I. The resulting t separated entries are nonzero powers of pi, and their image is a direct sum of t nonzero cyclic modules, each contributing one residue-field generator by Nakayama. This realizes every t including zero for the original A by reversing the coordinate changes. Balanced multiplicities give the global optimum n-ceil(n/(k+1)), also for n=1 and fields, and yield the k>=n-1 criterion at n>=2.
residual_risks: Finite test samples do not replace the argument for arbitrary finite chain rings or establish a classification of attainable full Smith shapes.

value.rationale: The zero-product sandwich is an established object and the generator count is its natural image-size invariant over a local ring. The exact formula sees the full Smith profile, explains the field/nonfield change, and detects precisely when an image can have n-1 generators. The witness and bound make the result useful without assuming a particular residue field or equal characteristic.
residual_risks: Only capacity is claimed; ruling on exact attainable Smith shapes or counting fibers would require additional work.
